land.text: Macedon, which the Roman republic 'divided ... into four client republics, called merides'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Antigonid Macedonia row ends 165; the antigonid-dynasty dossier ends the kingdom at Pydna in June 168.

land.text: Macedon, 'Rome's fifth provincia', created in autumn 148 BC (the lead and infobox say 146 BC)

successors.note: 'The date of the establishment of the province in autumn 148 BC is indicated by the epoch date of the provincial era'; the merides 'continued to exist as subdivisions of the province, as did the federal league'.

capitals.name: Amphipolis
capitals.note: One of the four merida capitals 'located at Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella, and Pelagonia'. Approximate coordinates of the site; the gazetteer has no Amphipolis.

capitals.name: Thessalonica (Thessaloniki)
capitals.note: A merida capital; 'The capital [of the province] was Thessalonica.'

capitals.name: Pelagonia (Bitola area)
capitals.note: A merida capital; the page names Pelagonia, not Heraclea. Coordinates are Bitola's, the region's modern centre.

correction.text: Macedon as the four merides (Macedonia page): 'divided Macedon into four client republics' with capitals at Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella and Pelagonia, members of 'the League of the Macedonians'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Antigonid Macedonia row runs to 165 and no row has the republics. The same Ancient Macedon region as roman-republic's 167 vassal event. The pages give neither the merides' boundaries nor an area; Epirus is not included (Rome enslaved 150,000 Epirotes in 167 and the Macedonia page puts Epirus inside the later province, not the republics).

correction.text: Macedon reunited as a kingdom by the pretender Andriscus: 'The kingdom was briefly reunited in 150 BC by the pretender Andriscus'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the shape is unchanged; the republics are overthrown for two years by Andriscus and the territory is contested (ledger 150-148). The pages do not say whether the merides' governments survived under him; the League of the Macedonians 'continued to exist' within the province afterwards. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' -149 to -148 so the last shape reaches the end year (province in autumn 148)]

ledger.note: 168: Rome replaces the Macedonian kingdom with four client republics. 'Macedon was to be divided into four merides' with capitals 'at Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella, and Pelagonia'; intermarriage between cantons banned, each paying 'a tribute which was half of what used to be paid to the king', gold and silver mining banned. The page places this after Pydna in 168; other dossiers (roman-republic) use 167.

168: the merides are Roman clients. They paid 'a tribute which was half of what used to be paid to the king' and the Third Macedonian War page says 'formal annexation was some years away'; the Macedonia page: 'client republics'.
150: Andriscus reunites the kingdom. 'The kingdom was briefly reunited in 150 BC by the pretender Andriscus.'
148: Metellus ends Andriscus's kingdom. 'After defeating Andriscus near Pydna in 148 BC' Rome made Macedonia 'Rome's fifth provincia'.
148: the republics become a province. 'The date of the establishment of the province in autumn 148 BC is indicated by the epoch date of the provincial era'; the lead gives 146 BC.

148: the merides end as states. They 'continued to exist as subdivisions of the province, as did the federal league' (page, undated); the province originally included Macedon, Paeonia, parts of Illyria and Thessaly, and Epirus (page, paraphrased), its capital Thessalonica.

wars.name: Fourth Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Andriscus reunited the kingdom in 150 and was 'defeated ... near Pydna in 148 BC' by Metellus; Macedonia became Rome's fifth province.
wars.note: The Macedonia page gives only Andriscus's reunion (150) and the defeat (148); the war's name is the usual Wikipedia title and is not quoted from that page.

certainty.note: No page gives the merides' boundaries; the shape is the Ancient Macedon region.

sources.title: Third Macedonian War
sources.note: The settlement after Pydna: four merides, capitals, tribute, bans (placed in 168; 'formal annexation was some years away').

sources.title: Macedonia (Roman province)
sources.note: Client republics, the League of the Macedonians, Andriscus 150, Metellus 148, province autumn 148 (lead 146), merides as subdivisions.

sources.title: Battle of Pydna
sources.note: 22 June 168; 'The Macedonian kingdom was dissolved, and its government was replaced with four republics'; no date for the republics.

notes: Three pages. The Third Macedonian War page puts the settlement in 168 and gives no 167 (the roman-republic dossier dates the vassal_start 167); the Pydna page dates the dissolution of the kingdom but not the republics; the Macedonia page dates neither. Start 168 follows the page; 167 is the usual date and one year apart changes nothing on the map. The end 148 follows the Macedonia page's body (autumn 148, provincial era) against its lead and infobox (146). The merides' own frontiers (the districts between the Nestos, Strymon, Axios and Peneus, and Pelagonia) are on none of the pages and are not drawn: one Ancient Macedon shape covers all four. The Macedonia page says the province originally included Macedon, Paeonia, parts of Illyria and Thessaly, and Epirus, i.e. more than the republics; those additions are roman-republic's 148 events. Andriscus (150-148) is only a counterpart string; two years is below the batch's ten-year threshold for a dossier. Mirrors: roman-republic /ledger 72 (vassal_start 167) and 75-76 (148) name 'Macedonian merides (four client republics)', which this slug now replaces; antigonid-dynasty ends 168 with the merides as successors by name only.
